page.layout: One column of running text, with four marginal notes in the left margin ("Cap.3.", "Cap.7.", "Cap.9.", "Cap.2."). Running head at top. Page number at top right. Catchword "lem" at the lower right, below the last line.

main_text.l: situm spiritum esse partis similaris formam
statuit. Nam nullo modo corporis forma
corpus esse potest, sed duntaxat corporis
naturalis pars essentialis, sicuti jam nos de
monstrauimus. His adde quod ipse libro
de Elementis formam corporis principiū
incorporeum profert. Quare forma per se
non potest esse corpus. Præterea mirari su-
bit, quomodo libro de Differentijs morbo-
rum Fernelius facultatem esse partis simi-
laris formam, & totam substantiam profe-
rat, & eodem secundo de Abditis rerum
causis, facultates corporum ab eorum sub-
stantijs, & formis ita aperte distinguat. Vis »
(inquit Eudoxus) & facultas imminui, au-
geriue potest, nonnunquam vero quasi im-
pedita teneri: substantia nulla ratione, vel
intendi, vel remitti potest. Hoc declarant
inueterata medicamenta, quorū vires pror-
sus infirmæ, & quasi eneruatæ iacent, for-
ma vero suaq; ipsorum substantia integra
etiamnum manet. Hæc Fernelius, quibus
nullam facultatem esse formam essentiale,
sed ab ipsa forma omnem proficisci palam
facit. Accedit huc illa facultatis definitio,
quam ille libro de Animæ facultatibus pro-
dit, qua nullam facultatem esse substantia-
Note: the "»" marks are the printed quotation marks of Eudoxus' speech running over several lines.

page.notes: The page begins with a fragment; the first letter of "situm" is partly cut off at the edge, so it is read as "situm" with the long s printed as f. The hyphenated word "substantia-" continues as "lem" in the catchword. Printed "fus" in "pror-fus" is the long s, read as "prorsus". Printed "si" and "s" are rendered as plain s throughout. "Cap.2." is set beside line 26, not the line that precedes it. No printing errors were corrected.
